speaker: Mikel Arteta
quote_text:
Hi guys, I've got the question. I'll come to you.  If we're ready, we'll go to Ed from the Guardian.  
I'm just wondering what the atmosphere's like  on changing rough that's quite difficult to pick  
them up on the ground. Yeah, very disappointed,  obviously very angry as well. I think you have  
to congratulate West Ham for the victory and the  game that they played. But as well, I think a lot  
from our side that we never got right and the end  allowed us to get enough momentum. enough sequence  
of play with positive action that could deliver  into situation of threat for there. And even  
though all the ball that we had and 20 shots of  that, I never felt that we were at the standards  
and the level that we needed, first of all, to  have more threat and then don't allow them to run  
because we lost a lot of balls that we allowed  West End to run in very dangerous positions.  
So when you say anger, it's anger yourself. Yeah,  yeah, yeah. We have to be. I hope we are very much  
because we didn't hit the levels Today, and I am  very much responsible of that, so I am very, very,  
very angry. I think people look at the forwards  and the injuries and think, Oh, that must be why.  
No, no, no, and I refuse that completely, because  I'm talking about the standards of the players  
and the team that we play today, me included, and  that was nowhere near the levels that we have to  
hit. to have the opportunity to win a Premier  League. Today, no. We were very consistent,  
yes, but football is about what you do today, and  today, nowhere near. Just on he said he seemed to  
be sort of limiting a bit when he came off. Is he  injured? No, hopefully not. It was just fatigue,  
I think. tom-tom, sorry, James, James, tom-tom. Hi  Michael, you mentioned you're not happy, you know,  
the level. You were very vocal, you know, in the  January, you felt you were short and Marina's up  
front today. Do you feel like the fact that there  was a struggle to score vindicates in some way  
why you were so vocal about wanting us? No, no,  no, no. Honestly, again, it's I think we have to  
look in the mirror of ourselves, of what we can do  better, what we've done that, and and the will and  
the desire and the way we run and the way we want  it, zero question about that. But at that level,  
this is not enough. You have to deliver and it has  to be with a lot of quality to break a really good  
team down, to win many more duets than we have  done, and to put actions that can end up in a  
really threatening moment for the position to win  the games, and today we haven't done that. What do  
you have to do now to change that game against  Florence? First of all, suffer. 24-48 hours.  
suffer and feel the pain and make sure that we  come back on Monday with that bite and that anger  
is still there in the tummy for Wednesday. James,  when you say you include, what do you think? No,  
me the first, sorry. If I said include. . . It's  my responsibility, the team, to play much better  
than we did today. Much better. We have to play  much better with much more person, much more  
quality, much more interaction, much more. Not  enough. That's on me. Do you think you got your  
team selection wrong? I wouldn't. I would do the  same. I would put it the same thing. But when you  
lose, you get it wrong. It is the tactics, the  intentions, everything. But that's what I felt.  
So I have to do what I feel after it's too late.  You said on Friday about being re-energised at the  
title race. Are you worried about the impact  that a result of this will have on the energy  
and the team to go again and go again and keep  believing? Hopefully a positive one, because  
it's already very negative what the result brings  and the consequences to that. So hopefully very  
positive that understand that we need to raise  the level. Before the game started, could you  
see the game falling the way it unfolded, or is  it sort of taking the basket? No, and especially  
the way we trained all week. No, but this is  football. Sometimes you see the warm-up and you  
see they are flat, then the game starts and we are  flying. I think the way we started the game and  
how imprecise we were with the ball and giveaways  and never got there, I think affected. But guys,  
we have 70, 80, 90 minutes to overcome that and we  certainly tried. But it wasn't enough today. How  
much is it down to what? That's the first thing  that I said, you know, and they see that we are  
not there and they start to have more belief and  they have the opportunity to run one or two times,  
go against the ball. In case you are out of  trouble when the situation is lucky, unlock  
the situation and then the spaces are open. You  have to do that and then before halftime there's  
a moment that we have them and suddenly they  score the goal and it gives It's the moral belief,  
so again, credit to them. Phil, I'm just going  back to the title race. Obviously, if four wins  
tomorrow, the gap will be 11 points. I mean,  do you think that sort of gap is manageable? Do  
you think that that's it in terms of in terms of?  It's not in our hands. For me, I'm really, really  
annoyed of the things that are in our hands that  we didn't do as well as we possibly could, and  
that's the performance and the result today. OK,  last couple for James. I'm for setting off. How do  
you interpret that incident? Any complaints from  you? No, I haven't seen it back, but honestly,  
I would focus on what we have to do. I don't know  if the decision was right or right. I haven't  
seen it. I don't want to evaluate it. But a lot of  the things that we should have done better today,  
it wasn't it wasn't it. Great season, but it's  still 18 years old. Is that a moment of maybe  
a bit of naivety there and a learning moment for  him? I don't know. I have to see the action back  
to evaluate it. OK, we got to go on for Rachel.  Just Mikael, on the fans, towards the end when  
you were pushing to score, there seemed like a lot  of frustration, particularly where I was sitting  
and anger. Did you feel that? And also, is that  something that can affect your players when you're  
pushing for a goal and you've got 10 men? Do you  need that support? And it felt like it was quite  
an anxious and furious atmosphere. I understand  as well that we won it and we are trying so hard  
and going against a lot of things and we had a  great opportunity today. and we don't deliver  
it. I think that's human. You asked me many times  what is the ideal and what the team needs and how  
we overcome certain deficiencies that we have in  this squad is them being in every single ball.  
That's my dream, but I'm not here to demand that  to the crowd. Okay, thank you. Yeah, thank you.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | Arsenal 0-1 West Ham United
